close_reason: Fixed in b045f70: chat-types AGENTS.md 'Settled Design Constraints' table now reads option-1 from the bead — minimal ::new() and named alternates where they enforce a type invariant or absorb required-field boilerplate. The earlier 'no ::new() methods' wording (predating extras-preservation policy) is retired.
description:
Trigger: a contributor reads crate-jmap-chat-types/AGENTS.md 'Design Constraints (Settled)' table:

    | Constructors | **None.** No ::new() methods in this crate. Construction
    |              | is the consumer's responsibility. Downstream crates use
    |              | serde_json deserialization to create instances. |

…then opens space.rs, chat.rs, message.rs, contact.rs, presence.rs, push.rs, position.rs, emoji.rs and finds ::new methods on Space, SpaceInvite, SpaceBan, Chat, Message, ChatContact, PresenceStatus, ChatMessagePush, ChatMessageEntry::plaintext, ChatMessageEntry::encrypted, ReadPosition, CustomEmoji. The crate-level rule and the implementation are in direct contradiction.

The ChatMessageEntry::encrypted constructor is independently useful — it enforces 'spec forbids body_snippet when encrypted' as a type invariant that struct-literal construction does not. That is good code.

The other ::new methods are mostly thin wrappers around struct-literal construction that exist to insulate callers from the 'extra' field. After commit 2957e6e adopted the extras-preservation policy, every struct grew a public 'extra: serde_json::Map<...>' field that the ::new methods all initialize to Map::new(). Removing the ::new methods would force callers to write '..Default::default()' or list 'extra: serde_json::Map::new()' inline, which is exactly the friction the ::new methods were meant to absorb.

Fix: pick ONE policy and edit both the AGENTS.md table and the source to match. Options:
1. Keep the constructors but rewrite the AGENTS.md row to: 'Constructors: minimal ::new() and named alternates where they enforce a type invariant or absorb required-field boilerplate. Otherwise prefer struct-literal construction.'
2. Remove all ::new() methods, derive Default where coherent, and document the 'extra: serde_json::Map::new()' boilerplate as the consumer's price for extras-preservation. (This is the harder path; it propagates pressure into jmap-chat-server and jmap-chat-client.)

Recommendation: option 1. The constructors are doing real work after extras-preservation landed; the AGENTS.md row is stale.

Priority P2 because the contradiction is a maintenance trap: a contributor following AGENTS.md literally would propose deleting all the ::new methods, the diff would be plausible, and the consumer breakage would surface only at the downstream crate. A clear written policy heads this off.
title: Construction policy: AGENTS.md says 'no ::new() methods', but the crate ships ::new() methods
